title: Little Office of the Suffering Christ, the Finding, and the Exaltation of the Holy Cross

introductoryNotes.text: From Devota Et Fructuosa Pietatis Exercitia Deum Triunum Adorandi (1751)

translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, Fili Dei vivi! qui hora sexta pro redemptione mundi crucis patibulum ascendisti, et sanguinem tuum pretiosum in remissionem peccatorum nostrorum fudisti: Te humiliter deprecamur, ut post obitum nostrum, Paradisi janua nos gaudenter introire concedas. Qui vivis, et regnas cum Deo Patre, etc.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, at the sixth hour you ascended the gibbet of the Cross for the redemption of the world and shed your precious blood for the remission of our sins. We humbly beseech you to grant that after our death we may enter joyfully through the gate of Paradise. You live and reign with God the Father, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus qui in praeclara salutiferae Crucis Inventione, Passionis tuae miracula suscitasti: concede, ut vitalis ligni pretio aeternae vitae suffragia consequamur. Qui vivis, et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O God, in the glorious Finding of the saving Cross you renewed the wonders of your Passion. Grant that through the price of the life-giving wood we may obtain the helps of eternal life. You live and reign, etc.
Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus qui nos hodierna die Exaltationis sanctae Crucis annua solemnitate laetificas: praesta, quaesumus, ut cujus mysterium in terra cognovimus, ejus redemptionis praemia in coelo mereamur. Per Dominum etc.
blocks.english: O God, you gladden us this day with the annual solemnity of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross. Grant, we pray, that we may be worthy in heaven of the rewards of the redemption whose mystery we have known on earth. Through the Lord, etc.
℣. Lord, you will open my lips, etc.
℟. And my mouth will proclaim, etc.
℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.
℟. Lord, to, etc.
℣ Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: English prepared directly for this printed Latin passage. A previously considered reused version had different versicle/response signs or expanded wording; the prepared English follows this office’s own signs and incipit. The source still awaits visual review.

blocks.english: Hymn (from Psalm 21)

blocks.source: Ego autem sum vermis, et non homo: opprobrium hominum, et abjectio plebis. Omnes videntes me, deriserunt me:
blocks.english:
But I am a worm and no man,
A reproach of men and an outcast of the people.
All who saw me mocked me:

blocks.source: locuti sunt labiis, et moverunt caput.
blocks.english: They spoke with their lips and shook their heads.
For February

blocks.source: ℣. Contritum est cor meum in medio mei,
blocks.english: ℣. My heart is broken within me.

blocks.source: ℟. Contremuerunt omnia ossa mea. Jerem. 23. v. 9. Oratio Domine Jesu Christe etc. ut supra.
blocks.english: ℟. All my bones trembled. Jeremiah 23:9. Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, etc., as above.

Hymn (from Psalm 21)

blocks.source: Tribulatio proxima est: quoniam non est, qui adjuvet. Circumdederunt me vituli multi: tauri pingues obsederunt me.
℣. Pater mi! si possibile est, transeat a me calix iste.
blocks.english: ℣. My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me.

blocks.source: ℟. Verumtamen, non sicut ego volo, sed sicut Tu.
blocks.english: ℟. Yet not as I will, but as you will.

blocks.source: Oratio Domine Jesu Christe ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Adoramus te Christe, et benedicimus tibi, Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℣. We adore you, Christ, and bless you, alleluia.

blocks.source: ℟. Quia per crucem tuam redemisti mundum, Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℟. For through your Cross you redeemed the world, alleluia.

blocks.source: ℣. O nobile lignum exaltatur, Christi fides rutilat.
blocks.english: ℣. O noble wood, it is exalted; the faith of Christ shines forth.

blocks.english: ℟. While the Cross is venerated by all.
℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.
Hymn (from Psalm 21)

blocks.source: Aperuerunt super me os suum, sicut leo rapiens et rugiens. Sicut aqua effusus sum, et dispersa sunt ossa mea: factum est cor meum tanquam cera liquescens in medio ventris mei.
blocks.english:
They opened their mouth against me
Like a ravening, roaring lion.
I am poured out like water,
And my bones are scattered.
My heart has become like wax,
Melting within me.

blocks.source: ℣. O vos omnes! qui transitis per viam, attendite:
blocks.english: ℣. O all you who pass along the way, attend:

blocks.source: ℟. Et videte, si est dolor, sicut dolor meus.
blocks.english: ℟. And see whether there is any sorrow like my sorrow.
Lamentations 1:12.

blocks.source: Oratio Domine Jesu Christe ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

blocks.english: ℣. O great work of loving mercy! Alleluia.

blocks.source: ℟. Mors mortua tunc est, in ligno quando mortua vita fuit, Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℟. Death itself died then, when Life died upon the wood, alleluia.
℣. We adore your Cross, Lord:
℟. And recall your glorious Passion.
℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.

blocks.source: Aruit tanquam testa virtus mea, et lingua mea adhaesit faucibus meis: et in pulverem mortis deduxisti me. Quoniam circumdederunt me canes multi: consilium malignantium obsedit me.

blocks.english: ℣. He gave his cheek to him who struck him:
℟. He was filled with reproaches.

blocks.source: Oratio Domine Jesu Christe, ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

blocks.english: ℣. Save us, Christ our Savior, alleluia.
℟. Through the power of the Holy Cross, alleluia.

blocks.english: ℣. This sign of the Cross shall be in heaven:

blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.
Hymn (from Psalm 21)

blocks.source: Foderunt manus meas, et pedes meos, et dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea, Ipsi vero consideraverunt; et inspexerunt me: diviserunt sibi vestimenta mea, et super vestem meam miserunt sortem.
blocks.english:
They pierced my hands and my feet
And numbered all my bones.
They themselves considered and gazed upon me;
They divided my garments among themselves
And cast lots for my clothing.

blocks.source: ℣. Sicut ovis ad occisionem ductus est:
blocks.english: ℣. Like a sheep he was led to slaughter:

blocks.source: ℟. Et quasi Agnus coram tondente se obmutuit.
blocks.english: ℟. And like a lamb before its shearer he was silent.
Isaiah 53:7.
Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

blocks.english: ℣. Behold the Cross of the Lord, alleluia.
℟. Flee, hostile powers, alleluia.
℣. O blessed Cross!

blocks.source: ℟. Quae sola digna fuisti portare Regem Coelorum.
blocks.english: ℟. You alone were worthy to bear the King of heaven.
℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.
Hymn (from Psalm 37)

blocks.source: Qui inquirebant mala mihi, locuti sunt vanitates, et dolos tota die meditabantur, Ego autem tanquam surdus non audiebam, et sicut mutus non aperiens os suum,
blocks.english:
Those who sought evil against me spoke vanities
And devised deceit all day long.
But I, like a deaf man, did not hear,
And like a mute man did not open my mouth.
℣. He humbled himself:

blocks.source: ℟. Factus obediens usque ad mortem, mortem autem Crucis. Philip. 2. v. 8.
blocks.english: ℟. Becoming obedient unto death, even death upon the Cross. Philippians 2:8.

blocks.source: Oratio Domine Jesu Christe, ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

blocks.english: ℣. But we ought to glory, alleluia.

blocks.source: ℟. In Cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi. Alleluia. Gal. 6. v. 4.
blocks.english: ℟. In the Cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, alleluia. Galatians 6:4 [as printed].
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints Galatians 6:4, retained here. The citation does not match the quoted sentence and requires source review.

blocks.english: ℣. Through wood we were made slaves:

blocks.source: ℟. Et per sanctam Crucem liberati sumus.
blocks.english: ℟. And through the Holy Cross we were set free.
℣. Turn us, O God, etc.
℣. O God, come to my assistance, etc.
Hymn (from Psalm 68)

blocks.source: Improperium exspectavit cor meum, et miseriam, et sustinui, qui simul contristaretur, et non fuit, et qui consoleretur, et non inveni, Et dederunt in escam meam fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto.
blocks.english:
My heart awaited reproach and misery;
I waited for one who would grieve with me, but there was none,
And for one who would comfort me, but I found none.
They gave me gall for my food,
And in my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.
℣. He delivered his soul unto death.

blocks.source: ℟. Et cum sceleratis reputatus est. Isaiae 53. 12.
blocks.english: ℟. And was counted among the wicked. Isaiah 53:12.

blocks.source: Oratio Domine Jesu Christe, ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, as above.

blocks.english: ℣. Through the sign of the Cross, alleluia.

blocks.source: ℟. De inimicis nostris libera nos Deus noster, Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℟. Deliver us from our enemies, our God, alleluia.
℣. At the touch of the Cross the dead rise:
℟. And may the mighty deeds of God be recounted.

blocks.source: Pro me care Jesu nate, Inque truces poenas date, Et cruenta vulnera. Da, o Jesu! ne tam dura Poena mortis et tortura Sit in nobis perdita.
blocks.english:
Dear Jesus, born for me,
Given over to savage punishments
And bloody wounds:
Grant, O Jesus, that such bitter
Punishment of death and torture
May not be wasted upon us.

blocks.source: Da, o Jesu! triste flere, De peccatis da dolere, Et patrata plangere. Patris iram, ne me perdant, Nec urendum orco tradant, Tuo seda sanguine. Amen.
blocks.english:
Grant, O Jesus, that I may weep in sorrow,
Grieve for my sins,
And mourn what I have done.
Lest they destroy me
And hand me over to burn in hell,
Calm the Father’s wrath with your blood. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.english: Commendation for May and September.

blocks.source: Ut Crux Christi contemnatur; Summi studet Tartarus; Nam qui ipsam aspernatur, Non est Dei Filius. Per torturam Jesu trucem Oro te, et vulnera, Cordi meo fige Crucem, Illa muni pectora. Amen.
blocks.english:
Hell strives with all its might
That Christ’s Cross be despised;
For whoever scorns it
Is not a child of God.
Through Jesus’ savage torture
And wounds I beseech you:
Fix the Cross in my heart;
With it fortify my breast. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.english: Sighs to the Suffering Christ.

blocks.source: O Domine Jesu Christe: adoro te, in cruce pendentem; coronam spineam in capite portantem: deprecor te, ut tua Crux liberet me ab Angelo percutiente. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! adoro te in cruce vulneratum, felle et aceto potatum: deprecor Te, ut vulnera tua sint remedium animae meae. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! rogo Te per illam amaritudinem passionis tuae, quam in hora mortis sustinuisti, maxime tunc, quando anima sanctissima de benedicto corpore tuo egressa est, miserere animae meae in egresso suo de corpore meo, et perduc eam in vitam aeternam. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! adoro te in sepulchro positum, mirha, et aromatibus conditum: deprecor te, ut tua mors sit vita mea. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! adoro te descendentem ad inferos, et tuos inde liberantem captivos: deprecor te, ut illuc nunquam me patiaris introire. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! adoro te, a mortuis resurgentem, et in Coelum ascendentem, sedentemque ad dexteram Patris: deprecor te, ut illuc te sequi, et tibi praesentari merear. Pater. Ave. O Domine Jesu Christe! Pastor bone! justos conserva, peccatores justifica, omnibus fidelibus miserere, et propitius etiam mihi misero et indigno peccatori. Pater. Ave.
blocks.english:
O Lord Jesus Christ, I adore you hanging upon the Cross, bearing the crown of thorns upon your head. I beseech you that your Cross may deliver me from the striking angel. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, I adore you wounded upon the Cross, given gall and vinegar to drink. I beseech you that your wounds may be a remedy for my soul. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, I ask you through that bitterness of your Passion which you endured at the hour of death, especially when your most holy soul departed from your blessed body: have mercy upon my soul at its departure from my body, and lead it into eternal life. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, I adore you laid in the tomb, embalmed with myrrh and spices. I beseech you that your death may be my life. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, I adore you descending to the underworld and freeing your captives from there. I beseech you never to permit me to enter there. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, I adore you rising from the dead, ascending into heaven, and sitting at the Father’s right hand. I beseech you that I may be worthy to follow you there and be presented to you. Our Father. Hail Mary.
O Lord Jesus Christ, good Shepherd, preserve the righteous, justify sinners, have mercy on all the faithful, and be merciful also to me, a wretched and unworthy sinner. Our Father. Hail Mary.
Prayer to God the Holy Spirit

blocks.source: Cognovi te Deum verum, et unum Spiritum Sanctum Patris, et Filii, ab utroque pariter procedentem, consubstantialem, et coaeternum Patri, et Filio, Paraclitum et Advocatum nostrum, qui super eundem Deum, et Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum in columbae specie descendisti, et super Apostolos in linguis igneis apparuisti: qui et omnes SS. et electos Dei a principio tuae gratiae numere docuisti, et ora Prophetarum; ut enarrent mirabilia Regni Dei, aperuisti: qui ab omnibus Sanctis Dei cum Patre, et Filio simul adoraris, et conglorificaris.
blocks.english: I have known you as true God, the one Holy Spirit of the Father and the Son, proceeding equally from both, consubstantial and coeternal with the Father and the Son, our Paraclete and Advocate. You descended in the likeness of a dove upon the same God and our Lord Jesus Christ, and appeared upon the apostles in tongues of fire. From the beginning you taught all the saints and elect of God by the gift of your grace, and opened the mouths of the prophets to recount the wonders of God’s kingdom. With the Father and the Son you are adored and glorified together by all the saints of God.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.source: Inter quos et ego servus tuus, et filius Ancillae tuae toto corde meo glorificabo nomen tuum, quoniam illuminasti me; Tu enim es vera Lux, et Lumen veridicum, ignis Dei, et Magister Spirituum, qui unctione tua, doces nos omnem veritatem, Spiritus veritatis, sine quo impossibile est placere Deo, quoniam tu ipse es Deus ex Deo, et Lux de luce, procedens a Patre Luminum ineffabiliter: et a suo Filio unico Domino nostro Jesu Christo: quibus consubstantialis, coaqualis, et coaeternus existens in unius Trinitatis essentia superessentialiter congloriaris, et conregnas.
blocks.english: Among them I too, your servant and the son of your handmaid, shall glorify your name with all my heart, for you have enlightened me. You are the true Light and truthful illumination, the fire of God and Teacher of spirits; by your anointing you teach us all truth, Spirit of truth, without whom it is impossible to please God. For you yourself are God from God and Light from Light, proceeding ineffably from the Father of lights and from his only Son, our Lord Jesus Christ. Being consubstantial, coequal, and coeternal with them in the essence of the one Trinity, you are glorified together and reign together in a manner beyond all essence.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.source: Cognovi te unum Deum, vivum, et verum, Patrem, et Filium, et Spiritum Sanctum, trinum quidem in personis, sed unicum in essentia, quem confiteor, adoro, et glorifico toto corde meo: verum Deum solum, sanctum, immortalem, invisibilem, incommutabilem, inaccessibilem, imperscrutabilem, unum lumen, unum solem, et unum panem, unam vitam, unum bonum, unum principium, unum finem, unum Creatorem Coeli terrae, per quem omnia vivunt, per quem omnia subsistunt, per quem omnia gubernantur, reguntur, et vivificantur, quae in caelis sunt, et quae in terris, et quae sub terra, praeterquam non est Deus in Coelo, et in terra.
blocks.english: I have known you as the one God, living and true, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit: three in persons, but one in essence, whom I confess, adore, and glorify with all my heart; the only true God, holy, immortal, invisible, unchangeable, inaccessible, unsearchable; one light, one sun, one bread, one life, one good, one beginning, one end, one Creator of heaven and earth, through whom all things live, through whom all things subsist, through whom all things are governed, ruled, and given life, in heaven, on earth, and beneath the earth; besides whom there is no God in heaven or on earth.
blocks.editorialNote: The source contains an irregular printed form; this prepared reading remains provisional and the Latin is retained unchanged.

blocks.source: Cognitor mei, sic cognovi te; cognovi te per fidem tuam, quam inspirasti mihi lux mea, lumen oculorum meorum, Domine Deus meus, spes omnium finium terrae, gaudium laetificans juventutem meam, et bonum sustentans senectutem meam. Amen.
blocks.english: You who know me, thus have I known you; I have known you through the faith in you which you inspired in me, my light, the light of my eyes, Lord my God, hope of all the ends of the earth, joy that gladdens my youth, and good that sustains my old age. Amen.

blocks.source: Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui dedisti famulis tuis in confessione verae fidei aeternae Trinitatis gloriam agnoscere; et in potentia Majestatis adorare Unitatem: quaesumus, ut ejusdem fidei firmitate ab omnibus semper muniamur adversis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, etc.
blocks.english: Almighty, everlasting God, you granted your servants, in the confession of the true faith, to acknowledge the glory of the eternal Trinity and to adore the Unity in the power of its majesty. We pray that by steadfastness in this same faith we may always be defended from all adversity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, etc.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. February, May and September alternatives and their distinct prayers remain printed in sequence; their calendar-dependent assembly is not automated. The Psalm excerpts remain excerpts.
